answers.question: What was the most recent significant change to the billing module's bill payment handling, and why was it made?

paragraphs.text: The most recent significant change to the billing module's bill-payment handling is **PR #155, "Payments should be associated with a cashier"** (commit `b52412a`, merged 1 April 2026, author Nethmi Rodrigo). It adds a `cashier` field to each payment so the system records *which* cashier took the money — the module's own README calls this "per-payment cashier attribution" [1].

Two caveats on why I picked it:
- It is the last change that alters the payment *model* and its validation. Newer commits do touch payments indirectly — #180 added refunds/discounts to receipts [1] and #182/#181 fixed a payment-status bug — but #155 is the substantive redesign of payment handling.
- The repository's pull requests were **not imported into Falkon** (`coverageGaps: "pull requests not ingested"`), so I could not read the PR description, linked tickets or review comments. The rationale below comes from the code, the commit message, and file comments, not from a ticket I read.

**Why it was made.** Before this change a payment recorded an amount, mode and tendered amount but nobody was attached to it. That left no accountability: given a completed payment you could not tell which cashier processed it. In OpenMRS a "cashier" is a `Provider` — a clinician/staff record linked to a person and a user account. The commit deliberately makes the cashier mandatory for *new* payments while tolerating old rows, so existing installations are not broken.

A telling detail: the same idea was attempted earlier in PR #109 (`edd6379`, ticket O3-5197) and reverted in #147 (`7dfc3af`). The difference between the two attempts is the reason #155 is significant — it is the version that learned not to reject pre-existing data. The first attempt rejected any payment without a cashier and hard-coded `provider_id="0"`/`"1"` into test datasets, which is exactly the pattern that breaks on databases with legacy payments. #155 instead exempts already-persisted payments.

- **Model** — a `Provider cashier` field was added to `Payment` [2], and mapped in Hibernate as a nullable many-to-one on the `provider_id` column of `cashier_bill_payment` [3].
- **Database** — Liquibase changeset `openmrs.billing-004-20260320-add-provider-id-to-bill-payment` adds a nullable `provider_id` with a foreign key to `provider`, `onDelete="SET NULL"` [4]. Nullable is intentional: it keeps legacy payments readable.
- **Validation** — `BillValidator.validateNewPaymentsHaveCashier` rejects a bill that carries a new, non-voided payment with no cashier, but skips payments that already have an id, i.e. legacy rows [5]. It is invoked from `validate` before the line-item check [6]. The ordering fix in the commit body explains why: the line-item check runs a DB query that makes Hibernate auto-flush transient payments, which would assign them ids and defeat the `id == null` test.
- **Auto-assignment on the REST layer** — when saving a bill, `BillResource` fills in the cashier from the authenticated provider for each new payment that has none, and raises a `RestClientException` if the logged-in user is not a provider [7]. The same fallback exists in `PaymentResource.save`, which throws an `APIException` when no provider is linked [8]. A client may still supply a cashier explicitly via the `cashier` property setter [9].
- **Shared lookup** — the change also removed duplicated cashier lookup code from `BillResource`, which now delegates to `ProviderUtil.getCurrentProvider` [10].

```mermaid
---
title: Cashier assignment on payment save
---
flowchart TD
    client["Client posts payment or bill"]
    resource["BillResource / PaymentResource"]
    current["ProviderUtil.getCurrentProvider"]
    check{"Cashier already set?"}
    error["Reject: user is not a provider"]
    set["payment.cashier = current provider"]
    validator["BillValidator.validateNewPaymentsHaveCashier"]
    legacy{"Payment already persisted?"}
    skip["Allowed for legacy data"]
    reject["Reject: paymentCashierRequired"]
    db["Persisted with provider_id"]

    client --> resource
    resource --> check
    check -->|yes| validator
    check -->|no| current
    current -->|null| error
    current -->|provider| set
    set --> validator
    validator --> legacy
    legacy -->|yes| skip
    legacy -->|no| reject
    skip --> db
    set --> db
```

- The PR bodies, tickets and review threads: pull requests for this repository were never imported, so the "why" rests on the code, commit message and comments rather than a ticket I read.
- The downstream effect on the O3 frontend. The payment representation now exposes `cashier` [11], and the API is a public REST contract, so the `openmrs-esm-billing-app` frontend may send or read it — I did not search that repository, so I cannot confirm how it consumes the new field.
- Whether tests elsewhere (e.g. integration datasets) still omit `provider_id`; the first attempt modified `BillTest.xml` for this, and I did not diff the full test suite for #155.
